answer: Randomized Wharf Assignment. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function assigns every active agent to one of many small work groups whose membership stays hidden until after commitments close; agents must complete a group task before their identity counts. An attacker cannot precompute which shale of identities will land together, so splitting into many sock puppets yields diminishing, unpredictable leverage. Registering N identities costs N task completions plus forfeited work when groups fail, and the fable of cheap mass registration breaks.
